- When sentiment is high (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% from prior 30d avg), model often overshoots; cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% above peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is falling, model underestimates drop; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast.
- Model consistently overpredicts mid-term (15–30d) prices when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.75); apply mean reversion to 15d window.
- When sentiment is uniformly high (all recent >0.75), model overfits upward trend; reduce forecast slope by 15–20%.
- If true outcome shows early reversal (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model fails to adjust; add 1–3% downward correction on day 4–6.
- Forecast should not exceed 1.5x prior 30d average unless sentiment >0.90 and confirmed breakout.
